objective: Attack the dominant PWP service cost by fetching two 256-bit rows per cycle while preserving M131 compact K4 correction ordering and exact W384 recurrence placement.

architecture_projection.candidate_requires: two independent 256-bit logical rows, equivalent dual-read behavior, or sixteen 32-bit bank words per service cycle

paper_safe_statement: On the frozen held-out W384 service-island recurrence, changing only PWP service from one to two 256-bit rows per cycle reduces exact PWP tokens by 47.20 percent and compact-K4 candidate cycles from 351,479,358 to 245,485,910, a 1.4318x module-cycle improvement and a 4.5415x same-clock ratio versus the frozen fixed8 service baseline. Dual-row/16-bank RTL, macro conflicts, area, energy, frequency, physical and system speedup remain unadmitted.
prohibited_claims: Do not call 4.5415x an end-to-end or full-network speedup.
Do not call 1.4318x a physical speedup before dual-row RTL and matched Synopsys evidence.
Do not treat two independent 256-bit rows per cycle as a free SRAM port.
Do not infer bank-conflict freedom, SRAM area, energy, or frequency from the cycle model.
Do not multiply the cycle ratio by any unreviewed frequency ratio.
Do not claim DATE best-paper or headline admission.
